title: A Colony for the Gravity
premise: Silas Dravenmoor, a memory-smuggler who trades in other people's pasts, intercepts a distress signal broadcast in a language extinct since the Sundering Wars. The signal comes from the Halcyon, a derelict cryo-ark holding two frozen colonies: one descended from the war's victors, one from its condemned. A customs tribunal offers Silas amnesty if she helps them wake only the victors' descendants and erase the rest; her own smuggled memories hold the proof that the condemned were innocent. Silas chooses truth over loyalty to the guild that raised her, wakes both colonies, and broadcasts the archived memories system-wide — ending her smuggling career but beginning a reckoning two centuries overdue.
about_author: Emrys Voss is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. Voss writes near-future science fiction about people who move through systems quietly, until they can't.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Living
chapters.summary: Silas runs a routine memory-smuggling pass through contested orbit, establishing her world: the guild that raised her, the tribunal's tightening grip, and her rule never to open what she carries. The extinct-language signal interrupts a handoff. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: restless competence cracked open by wonder — for the first time in ten years, she opens the cargo.

chapters.title: The Ark That Remembers
chapters.summary: Silas traces the signal to the Halcyon and discovers the twin cryo-colonies and the tribunal's plan to wake only half. Her guild handler, Maren, orders her to walk away; the tribunal offers amnesty for her silence. POV: Silas, with flashback fragments from smuggled memories. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. conscience — she realizes the guild knew about the ark all along.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Silas breaks into the Halcyon's archive core and finds the condemned colony's innocence recorded in smuggled memory-chips she herself once carried without reading. Tribunal enforcers board; Maren betrays her position to save the guild. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizes her choice — she initiates the wake sequence for both colonies as the hull is breached.

chapters.title: A Reckoning in Cold Light
chapters.summary: As colonists wake, Silas broadcasts the archive to every station in contested orbit, sacrificing her anonymity and freedom. The tribunal fractures; Maren, facing exposure, chooses at last to testify. Silas surrenders to the new joint council — not as a criminal, but as a witness. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: costly resolution — justice outside the law achieved, paid for with everything she was.
